_comment: Reads SwiftUI's .grayscale luminance basis directly off the render. filter: grayscale(100%) on a pure primary outputs that channel's weight x 255, so these four components DISCRIMINATE between the candidate bases rather than merely agreeing with one: Rec.709-gamma predicts 54/182/18/75, Rec.601-gamma predicts 76/150/29/79, and a linear-space sum predicts 127/220/76/82. Measured on iOS: 54/182/18/75 (Rec.709 gamma, exact on all four). SepiaMatrix.swift depends on this fact, so it is pinned here where anyone can re-measure it.
_expect_comment: _expect schema v1 (inert to rendering; enforced by the spec oracle): fill.rgb = dominant non-page-background capture colour (ground is rgb(26,26,46)); fill.tol = per-channel absolute tolerance; box = declared CSS px (1 CSS px = 1 capture px everywhere). Derivation, recomputed from filter-effects-1 8.5: grayscale(100%) collapses every channel to 0.2126R + 0.7152G + 0.0722B on gamma-encoded sRGB. Red: 0.2126*255 = 54.213 -> 54. Green: 0.7152*255 = 182.376 -> 182. Blue: 0.0722*255 = 18.411 -> 18. Mixed #804020 = (128,64,32): 27.213 + 45.773 + 2.310 = 75.296 -> 75. tol is 0 on all four DELIBERATELY: floor and round agree on every value (no fractional part near .5), the committed baselines are exact on all three platforms, the A/A noise floor is zero, and the fixture's whole purpose is discriminating bases 20+ steps apart — any slack would only dilute that.
